item.title: The R&B Club Discusses The Legacy of Aaliyah — Sun Aug 23, 12:00 PM — Songbyrd
item.description: Certain moments in this century have stayed with us. And they always will. August 25, 2001, is just that. It seems almost surreal to say, but The R&B Club’s next event comes almost a quarter-century to the day that the R&B icon Aaliyah tragically passed away. There's no way not to have a connection to her music, but more importantly, Aaliyah herself. If you know anything about us, and what we pride ourselves on, this won't be simply music being played. This is a voyage and a trip back in time into one of the most captivating and abbreviated careers in music history. We’ll discuss it all. The highs, the classic records, where we were when we got the news of her death — and, yes, the R. Kelly of it all. It's one time for Babygirl (better known as Aaliyah) on Sunday, August 23, at the only home we've ever known in Songbyrd. Tickets are $15 in advance and $20 at the door — pending there's any left. item.title: Staring in Spaces (Single Release Show) — Sat Oct 10, 7:00 PM — Songbyrd
item.description: Saturday October 10th Staring in Spaces (Single Release Show) w/ Endlings \+ FREE after party w/ DJ FIBI and Yoshmo! \*\*\* Staring in Spaces: The pop duo bringing infectious energy to the Nation's Capital. Childhood friends Jack Wright and William Lorenz began their musical journey in small-town Wisconsin, quickly gaining momentum with their debut album Stop Talking. Now settled in D.C., Staring in Spaces released their boldest and most ambitious album yet, Kissing!, at the end of 2024. Featuring standout singles like the punchy "my mom/your dad" and the nostalgic "Postcard," the album pushes their pop sensibilities into rougher textures and edgier performances. With a successful tour behind them and energized audiences craving more. Wright and Lorenz are diving headfirst into 2026. \*\*\* Endlings are four friends making music at the event horizon. item.description: Thursday September 10th ZACK KEIM x GARDENER w/ THE DUSKWHALES, STEPHEN SOL \*\*\* ZACK KEIM His second solo album, titled “Battery Lane” is out now via Evan Westfall of Caamp’s indie label Super Sport Records. Named after the street where Keim lived during his time in the DC area, the album reflects the people and places that inspired this chapter of his songwriting. From 2025 to 2026, he toured extensively throughout the US/Europe/and UK. Keim's powerful live performances have led him to play SXSW and share the stage with renowned artists such as Peter Case (The Nerves/Plimsouls), indie icon Calvin Johnson (Beat Happening/founder of K Records), and acclaimed singer-songwriter Matt Costa. His standout single, “Better Days,” has received praise from Sirius XMU calling it “a fun, fuzzy, classic.” GARDENER Hailing from Yellow Springs, OH, Gardener is a close-knit group of old friends. Their music paints vivid sonic landscapes, blending raw Americana with dreamy, country-tinged indie rock

item.title: Spoonfed (EP Release Show) — Fri Sep 25, 7:00 PM — Songbyrd
item.description: Friday September 25 Spoonfed (Single Release Show) w/ The Montaines, Aidan Leclaire \*\*\* Spoonfed is a Washington, D.C.-based rock band consisting of Will Sevy (vocals/guitar), Kevin Cox (bass), and Kieran O'Dell (vocals/drums). Formed in 2021 in the basement of their house in Charlottesville, Virginia, Spoonfed has grown from late-night jam sessions into one of the DMV's emerging indie bands. Spoonfed draws inspiration from the grunge rock of the 1990s, the alt-rock of the early 2000s, and the grooves of modern funk. Expect energy: dark and uplifting melodies, dynamic rhythms, moody lyrics, guitar solos. Their debut EP drops September 16. \*\*\* Described as delivering “sticky guitar riffs and romantic songs that sound like they belong on a 2014 Tumblr playlist,” the band’s live show is nothing short of exhilarating. item.title: JOZZY: GET HER BACK TOUR — Mon Sep 28, 7:00 PM — Songbyrd
item.description: Before the world knew her name, they knew her pen. Jozzy is the Diamond certified, three time Grammy nominated singer songwriter from Memphis, Tennessee, whose catalog has generated over two billion streams across credits for Beyoncé, SZA, Summer Walker, Lil Nas X, Drake, Metro Boomin, Mary J. Blige, and dozens more. She co wrote the Billy Ray Cyrus verse that turned "Old Town Road" into the fastest Diamond certified song in RIAA history. She gave Beyoncé "Virgo's Groove." She penned Summer Walker's "Body" and SZA's "Low." She scored Spider Man: Across the Spider Verse. Raised in the lineage of Memphis soul royalty, her mother sang alongside Al Green and Ann Peebles at Hi Records. Jozzy honed her craft under the mentorship of Timbaland and Missy Elliott before becoming one of the most commercially impactful writers of her generation. item.title: Guerilla Toss — Tue Oct 20, 7:00 PM — Songbyrd
item.description: When NYC-based experimental dance punks Guerilla Toss, active since time immemorial aka 2011, were in Vermont recording their new full-length album You’re Weird Now, frontwoman Kassie Carlson would prepare what she called ‘punk lunch’: a communal meal made by raiding the studio fridge for whatever was left and assembling a sandwich from the most random ingredients imaginable. Regularly joining punk lunch were two legends from their own corners of the weird music world: Stephen Malkmus (Pavement, The Jicks) and Trey Anastasio, Phish guitarist and owner of The Barn; the recording studio where Guerilla Toss were making You’re Weird Now, with Malkmus in the producer’s seat. Engineer Bryce Goggin, who has worked with Malkmus since Crooked Rain, Crooked Rain, and Ben Collette, Phish’s longtime engineer at The Barn, were also part of the crew. item.title: Renny Conti - Split Second Tour — Sun Oct 25, 7:00 PM — Songbyrd
item.description: Sunday October 25th Renny Conti w/ James Eichman \*\*\* Through his early twenties, Renny self-released a string of homemade albums, sorting out his aesthetic and narrative viewpoint as a musician before his project began in earnest. His self-titled debut was recorded in 2023, collecting older material that served as a proper introduction to him as an artist. Finally released in 2025, the album soon earned him buzz across the indie landscape, and landed him a deal with Mom+Pop. Once more, Split Second feels like a long-awaited debut: Emerging from not only 2023 but all the years before, Split Second catalogues the snapshots and places and people that made Renny the musician he is today. Renny’s life in music began as it does for many of us: a means of escape from the confusing pivot from childhood to teenage years. item.description: Saturday October 24th Songbyrd x U+N Booking Present Swapmeet is a 4-piece band from South Australia composed of Venus O’Broin (guitar, vocals), Joshua Doherty (bass), Maxwell Elphick (guitar, drums, vocals), and Jack Medlyn (guitar, drums, vocals). Having recently caught the ear of American indie label Winspear, the band is readying their debut album and offering a taste of the new material with “I Know!”, a cathartic and buoyant debut single for their new label home. Revved up with gleaming, fuzzy guitars and energetic percussion, the new track blurs jangle pop, shoegaze, and alt-rock with tongue-in-cheek precision. The group met as teenagers in the early 2020s while playing in various projects around the Adelaide music scene and bonded over their love of 90s alternative, citing Pavement and Sonic Youth as early influences.
